title: Finite-coefficient unbounded classical essential image
statement:
Let $k$ be a finite or algebraically closed field, let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $k$, and let $A$ be a finite commutative ring annihilated by $\ell^r$ for some $r\geq1$. Let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Use ordinary constant-coefficient module sheaves, the unbounded derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], and the comparison morphism $
u_X:X_{\mathrm{proet}}	o X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], with exact termwise inverse image $
u_X^*$ and total unbounded direct image $R
u_{X,*}$ computed by K-injective resolutions [def-pur-kinjective-complex], so that $
u_X^*\dashv R
u_{X,*}$ on these unbounded categories. Write $D_{\mathrm{class}}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ for the full subcategory of $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ of complexes whose cohomology sheaves are classical in the sense of [sk-def-pe-classical-definition]. Then $
u_X^*$ maps $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ into $D_{\mathrm{class}}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, and for every $K\in D_{\mathrm{class}}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, with no boundedness assumption, the counit $
u_X^*R
u_{X,*}K	o K$ is an isomorphism. In particular every object of $D_{\mathrm{class}}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ is isomorphic to $
u_X^*M$ for some $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$.

source.place: Proposition 5.2.6 (3), Remark 5.2.8, Definition 5.3.1 and Proposition 5.3.2 (pp. 37-38): when D(X_et) is left-complete (locally finite cohomological dimension) the unbounded pullback identifies D(X_et) with D_cc(X_proet); specialized to finite l-primary coefficients and finite-type schemes over finite or algebraically closed fields; blueprint sk-prop-pe-unbounded-classical (finite-coefficient hypotheses)

proof.text: Write $F=\nu_X^*$ and $R=R\nu_{X,*}$. The inverse image is exact termwise, so [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below] gives that for every $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ one has $H^q(FM)\cong F(H^qM)$ for every $q$. The module part of the classical-sheaf comparison says that $F(H^qM)$ is a classical $A$-module sheaf. Hence $F$ maps the whole unbounded étale derived category into the full subcategory of complexes with classical cohomology.

If $X$ is empty, the empty-cover sheaf condition forces every module sheaf on either site to be zero, so all the conclusions hold. Assume henceforth that $X$ is nonempty, and put $e=2\dim(X)+1\geq0$. Every $A$-module sheaf is annihilated by $\ell^r$, hence is torsion. Applying [det-pe-unbounded-classical-bounds] with $g=\mathrm{id}_X$ gives $H^q(U_{\mathrm{proet}},(F G)|_U)=0$ for $q>e$ whenever $G$ is an étale $A$-module sheaf and $U$ has a pro-étale affine presentation over $X$. In particular this holds for every affine étale $W\to X$, using its constant presentation. By the module-sheaf essential-image statement of [sk-thm-pe-classical-sheaves], every classical $A$-module sheaf is isomorphic to $F G$, so the same bound holds for every classical coefficient sheaf, with the same $e$ independent of $W$.

source.place: statement, parts (1) and the sentence that the same statements hold with X replaced by Y

proof.text: If $K\in D^+_{\mathrm{class}}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, the bounded-below unit supplied by [sk-prop-sf-comparison] satisfies the hypothesis of [det-pe-classical-derived-equivalence]. Its part (2) therefore gives that the counit $F R K\to K$ is an isomorphism. Thus the desired counit is already known on all bounded-below classical complexes. The unbounded right derived functor used here restricts to the bounded-below one: by [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution] a bounded-below representative has a bounded-below injective resolution which is also K-injective, and this same resolution computes both right derived functors and their adjunction counits.

For $K\in D_{\mathrm{class}}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and $m\in\mathbf Z$, let $P_m(K)$ be the presheaf on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ given by $W\mapsto H^mR\Gamma(W,K)$, where $R\Gamma(W,-)$ is total derived evaluation on the pro-étale site. There is a natural identification $H^m(RK)=P_m(K)^\#$. Indeed, the pro-étale site is taken in its small skeleton and $A_{X,\mathrm{proet}}$ is a sheaf of commutative rings, so [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] gives every complex of $A$-module sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ a K-injective resolution; this is the existence hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] and of the stipulated computation of $R$. Choose a K-injective representative $I$ of $K$. By the stipulated computation of $R$ and the restriction formula in [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], $RK$ is represented by the étale sheaf complex $W\mapsto I(W)$. [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] also makes $I$ compute total derived evaluation at every $W$. Its underlying presheaf cohomology is $W\mapsto H^m(I(W))=P_m(K)(W)$. Exact sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact] identifies the sheafification of this cohomology presheaf with the cohomology sheaf of that complex. For a derived morphism choose a chain-map representative between K-injective resolutions, using [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]; chain-homotopic representatives induce the same section cohomology maps. Thus the identification is natural, including for every truncation map used next.

source.place: Remark 5.2.8, reduction to bounded-below complexes, made explicit using the blueprint fixed-degree truncation estimate; Proposition 5.3.2 for the classical subcategory

proof.text:
Fix $m$ and choose an integer $N<m-e-1$. Put $T=\tau_{\geq N}K$ and let $t:K\to T$ be the canonical map. Its cohomology is zero below $N$ and agrees with that of $K$ in degrees at least $N$, so $T$ is bounded below and classical, and $H^m(t)$ is an isomorphism. For every affine étale $W\to X$, step 2 verifies precisely the classical-sheaf hypothesis of [det-pe-unbounded-classical-truncation]; part (2) makes $P_m(t)(W)$ an isomorphism. The kernel and cokernel presheaves of $P_m(t)$ are therefore zero on every affine étale object. If $Q$ is either of these presheaves and $S$ any étale sheaf, every map $Q\to S$ is zero: its value on a section restricts to zero on an affine open cover of its domain, hence is zero by the sheaf condition. The universal property of sheafification gives $\operatorname{Hom}(Q^\#,S)=0$ for every $S$, so $Q^\#=0$. Exact sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact] now makes both the kernel and cokernel of $P_m(t)^\#$ zero, so this map is an isomorphism. Step 4 gives that $H^m(Rt)$ is an isomorphism, and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below] then makes $H^m(FRt)$ an isomorphism. Counit naturality gives
$$H^m(t)\circ H^m(\varepsilon_K)=H^m(\varepsilon_T)\circ H^m(FRt).$$
The right side is an isomorphism by step 3, and $H^m(t)$ is an isomorphism, so $H^m(\varepsilon_K)$ is an isomorphism. The integer $m$ was arbitrary; [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] proves that the actual counit $\varepsilon_K:FRK\to K$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Remark 5.2.8, reduction to bounded-below complexes, made explicit using the blueprint fixed-degree truncation estimate; Proposition 5.3.2 for the classical subcategory

proof.text: The counit is therefore an isomorphism in the derived category. Since $R K$ is an object of $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, every $K$ in the classical pro-étale subcategory is isomorphic to $F(RK)$, proving the final essential-surjectivity clause.

The exact classical image and uniform torsion bounds are retained. No new nodes, Mathlib leaves, or statement change.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the opening classical-comparison sentence of sk-lem-geo-affine-local: the exact classical image (step 1), finite torsion bounds of sk-prop-pe-unbounded-classical (step 2), bounded-below counit (step 3), and fixed-degree truncation reduction of Bhatt–Scholze Remark 5.2.8 (steps 4–5), with the essential-surjectivity consequence (step 6). Full faithfulness and unbounded direct-image comparison remain separate existing nodes.

The coefficients are A-module sheaves over the constant ring and nu_X is the site comparison, as in sk-prop-sf-comparison and det-pe-classical-derived-equivalence. Steps check out: (1) classical image via the exact-functor cohomology formula plus the sk-thm-pe-classical-sheaves essential image; (2) uniform e=2dimX+1 from bounds(1) with g=id, using the constant presentation of affine etale W and torsion from l^r A=0, with the empty X handled; (3) D^+ counit, where bounded-below injective complexes are K-injective so the two R agree; (4) H^m(RK)=P_m(K)^# by nu_*I(W)=I(W) and exact sheafification, natural through K-injective Hom; (5) N<m-e-1 gives truncation (2) on affine W, the kernel/cokernel presheaves sheafify to 0 because of affine covers, and the counit naturality square plus the cohomology criterion finish; (6) elementary. Edge cases tested: X empty, A=0, K=0, K bounded below, K in one degree, K unbounded below, X a point. No new nodes, no duplicate in the DAG or in blueprint main-20261015, no SGA.
